natural: an old well with no ripples

meaning.en: A mind so calm that nothing stirs it; completely unmoved by emotion or temptation.
meaning.zh: 心像古井里的水一样不起波澜，形容心情非常平静，不为外界所动。

examples.zh: 经历了这么多风波，他如今心中古井无波。
examples.en: After so many ups and downs, his heart is now perfectly calm.

examples.zh: 面对同事的挑衅，她古井无波，只是笑了笑。
examples.en: Faced with her colleague's provocation, she stayed unruffled and merely smiled.

usage.en: Usually describes a person's inner state; predicate or attributive. Literary tone.
usage.zh: 多形容人的心境，作谓语、定语，书面语色彩较浓。

story.en: Meng Jiao's poem on the faithful woman ends 'My heart is an old well, its waves vowed never to rise' (波澜誓不起，妾心古井水). The idiom 'still water in an old well' for a mind that nothing disturbs derives from this image.
story.zh: 孟郊《列女操》云：“梧桐相待老，鸳鸯会双死。贞女贵殉夫，舍生亦如此。波澜誓不起，妾心古井水。”后以“古井无波”比喻心境平静，不为外物所动。

meaning.en: A polite way of saying that one does not think much of something or someone.
meaning.zh: 委婉地表示不佩服、不赞同，实际上是说不怎么样。

equivalents: not much to write home about

examples.zh: 这家餐厅的服务态度，我实在不敢恭维。
examples.en: I can't honestly praise the service at this restaurant.

examples.zh: 他的球技我可不敢恭维，十次投篮只进了一次。
examples.en: I can't say much for his basketball; he sank only one shot in ten.

usage.en: Understatement: the speaker is actually criticising. Often follows 实在 or 可 and takes 对…, or 我…不敢恭维.
usage.zh: 说话人用客气的口气表达批评，常说“实在不敢恭维”“我对……不敢恭维”。

meaning.en: Poor eyesight in old age; also used humbly for one's own mistakes of perception.
meaning.zh: 年老眼睛看不清楚；也常用来自谦，表示自己看错了。

equivalents: can't see as well as I used to

examples.zh: 爷爷老眼昏花，看报纸得戴老花镜。
examples.en: Grandpa's eyesight has dimmed with age; he needs reading glasses for the paper.

examples.zh: 我老眼昏花，把数字看错了，抱歉。
examples.en: My old eyes deceived me and I misread the figure; sorry.

usage.en: Often self-mocking when said about oneself. Predicate or attributive.
usage.zh: 自称时带自嘲或自谦的口气，多作谓语、定语。

natural: hold an army to make oneself weighty

meaning.en: To use control of an army to build up one's own power and refuse to obey the central authority.
meaning.zh: 掌握军队，凭借武力抬高自己的地位，不服从中央。

equivalents: use military strength to hold the government to ransom

examples.zh: 东汉末年，不少州牧拥兵自重，各霸一方。
examples.en: At the end of the Eastern Han, many governors kept their own armies and ruled their own domains.

examples.zh: 历史上，拥兵自重的将领往往成为朝廷的心腹之患。
examples.en: In history, generals who hoarded their armies often became a thorn in the court's side.

usage.en: Usually about warlords or generals; can be extended figuratively to anyone who leverages power for self-interest. Verb phrase.
usage.zh: 多指军阀、将领，也可比喻凭借实力抬高自己的人，作谓语。

pinyin: jǐ jiā huān lè jǐ jiā chóu
literal: how many · households · happy · how many · households · sad

meaning.en: At the same moment some people are happy while others are sad; fortunes differ.
meaning.zh: 同一时间里，有的人家欢乐，有的人家忧愁，指各人境遇不同、悲喜各异。

equivalents: one man's meat is another man's poison

examples.zh: 高考放榜，几家欢乐几家愁。
examples.en: When the exam results came out, some families were delighted and others dejected.

examples.zh: 股市大涨大跌，几家欢乐几家愁。
examples.en: With the market swinging wildly, some investors rejoice while others weep.

usage.en: Often used as a comment on results, rankings, or markets. Said in full or with 有人…有人….
usage.zh: 常用来评论考试、比赛、股市等结果，多整句使用。

synonyms: 大风吹倒梧桐树——有人欢喜有人愁

meaning.en: To be so stirred that one's mind cannot settle, typically through excitement, attraction or temptation.
meaning.zh: 心里像旗子在风中摇动，形容心神不定、情绪激荡。

examples.zh: 一听到那个消息，他不禁心旌摇荡，彻夜难眠。
examples.en: On hearing the news he was deeply stirred and couldn't sleep all night.

examples.zh: 面对美景，她心旌摇荡，久久不愿离去。
examples.en: Before the lovely view she felt her heart swell and lingered a long time.

usage.en: Literary; the feeling can be joyful or tempting. Often 令人心旌摇荡.
usage.zh: 书面语，所指的心情可以是欣喜，也可以是被诱惑，常说“令人心旌摇荡”。

natural: the joy of the swallows' move

meaning.en: Congratulations on moving into a new home or premises.
meaning.zh: 祝贺人迁入新居或新址的贺词。

examples.zh: 恭贺张先生燕徙之喜，愿新居福气满堂。
examples.en: Congratulations to Mr Zhang on his new home; may it be full of blessings.

examples.zh: 公司搬进新大楼，同行纷纷送来花篮，祝贺燕徙之喜。
examples.en: As the company moved into its new building, peers sent flower baskets to congratulate it.

usage.en: A formal greeting for housewarming cards and banners; 徙 is read xǐ. Equivalent to 乔迁之喜.
usage.zh: 用于新居落成、迁居的贺词，“徙”读xǐ，与“乔迁之喜”同义。

meaning.en: The bond between a mother and her child is so close that each feels the other's pain.
meaning.zh: 母亲和孩子心意相通，一方有难，另一方就会感到痛苦。

equivalents: mother and child are of one heart

examples.zh: 母子连心，孩子在外地受了伤，妈妈半夜就睡不着了。
examples.en: Mother and child are one in heart; when her son was hurt far away, she woke in the middle of the night.

examples.zh: 都说母子连心，他一进门，母亲就知道他心里有事。
examples.en: They say mother and child are of one heart; the moment he entered, his mother knew something was wrong.

usage.en: Often said of intuition or emotional closeness between mother and child. Neutral, warm tone.
usage.zh: 多用来说母亲与孩子之间的心灵感应、亲情深厚，语气温暖。

natural: repay a grudge with a grudge

meaning.en: To answer a wrong with a wrong; to retaliate in kind.
meaning.zh: 用怨恨来回报怨恨，指别人对自己不好，自己也以不好的方式回报。

equivalents: give as good as one gets

examples.zh: 冤家宜解不宜结，以怨报怨只会让仇恨越积越深。
examples.en: Feuds should be settled, not stoked; repaying grudge with grudge only deepens hatred.

examples.zh: 他不愿以怨报怨，选择原谅了对方。
examples.en: He refused to hit back in kind and chose to forgive.

usage.en: Often contrasted with 以德报怨 or 以直报怨. Usually advice against it.
usage.zh: 常与“以德报怨”“以直报怨”对照，多作劝诫。

meaning.en: Time spares nobody; people inevitably age and decline.
meaning.zh: 时间不会宽恕任何人，人总要变老、衰退。

equivalents: time and tide wait for no man
the years catch up with everyone

examples.zh: 岁月不饶人，我跑几步就喘了。
examples.en: The years spare no one; I'm out of breath after a few steps.

examples.zh: 看着老同学满头白发，才感叹岁月不饶人。
examples.en: Seeing my old classmate's white hair, I sighed that time spares nobody.

usage.en: A sigh about ageing; often with 真是 or 都说. Casual.
usage.zh: 多用于感叹年老体衰，口语常说“真是岁月不饶人”。

pinyin: cái lí hǔ kǒu, yòu rù láng wō
literal: just · leave · tiger · mouth, again · enter · wolf · den
natural: just out of the tiger's mouth, into the wolf's den

meaning.en: To escape one danger only to fall into another.
meaning.zh: 刚摆脱一个危险，又陷入另一个危险。

equivalents: out of the frying pan into the fire

examples.zh: 他刚逃出赌场的债务，又被骗进了传销，真是才离虎口，又入狼窝。
examples.en: He had barely escaped his gambling debts when he was lured into a pyramid scheme: out of the tiger's mouth into the wolf's den.

examples.zh: 换了一家公司，老板更苛刻，简直才离虎口，又入狼窝。
examples.en: The new company's boss is even harsher: out of the frying pan into the fire.

usage.en: Often with 真是 or 简直. Casual.

natural: a loyal liver and righteous gall

meaning.en: Utterly loyal and chivalrous; ready to give everything for loyalty and justice.
meaning.zh: 形容对人忠诚，讲义气，不惜付出一切。

equivalents: heart of gold and true as steel

examples.zh: 关羽忠肝义胆，千古传颂。
examples.en: Guan Yu's loyalty and righteousness have been praised through the ages.

examples.zh: 他对朋友忠肝义胆，从不退缩。
examples.en: He is fiercely loyal to his friends and never shrinks back.

usage.en: Praises a person's character; attributive or predicate. Liver and gall stand for courage and sincerity.
usage.zh: 赞扬人的品格，作定语、谓语。肝、胆比喻真诚和勇气。

natural: a rich country and a strong army

meaning.en: A nation that is wealthy and militarily powerful.

examples.zh: 商鞅变法的目标是使秦国国富兵强。
examples.en: The aim of Shang Yang's reforms was to make Qin rich and strong.

examples.zh: 只有国富兵强，才不会被人欺负。
examples.en: Only a rich and strong nation will not be bullied.

usage.en: Used in writing about statecraft and history. Predicate or attributive.
usage.zh: 多用于谈论治国和历史，作谓语、定语。

literal: not · fall into · words · fish trap
natural: not fall into the trap of words

meaning.en: To grasp the real meaning without being bound by the words used to express it.
meaning.zh: 不拘泥于语言文字，直接领会其中的真意。

equivalents: get the spirit, not the letter

examples.zh: 读诗要不落言筌，体会作者的真情。
examples.en: When reading poetry, don't get stuck on the words; feel the poet's true emotion.

examples.zh: 这位老师讲课不落言筌，总能点出要害。
examples.en: This teacher never gets bogged down in wording and always hits the heart of the matter.

usage.en: Literary; often about reading, Zen, or art criticism. 筌 is a bamboo fish trap, read quán.
usage.zh: 书面语，多用于读书、禅理、评论艺术。“筌”是捕鱼的竹器，读quán。

pinyin: shēn jiào shèng yú yán jiào
natural: teaching by example beats teaching by words

meaning.en: Setting an example teaches better than preaching.
meaning.zh: 以自己的行动作榜样，比口头教导更有效。

examples.zh: 身教胜于言教，父母爱读书，孩子自然也爱读书。
examples.en: Example beats instruction: if parents love reading, their children will too.

examples.zh: 作为老师，要明白身教胜于言教。
examples.en: As a teacher, you must understand that example beats lecturing.

usage.en: Common in education and parenting advice. Neutral.
usage.zh: 常用于教育、家教方面的劝勉，中性。

natural: thoughts of the Hao and the Pu rivers

meaning.en: A yearning for the carefree seclusion of nature, free of worldly cares.
meaning.zh: 像庄子在濠水、濮水边那样，想隐逸山水、逍遥自在。

equivalents: a longing for the simple life
a yen for the country idyll

examples.zh: 一到溪边，他便生出濠濮间想。
examples.en: On reaching the stream he felt a pull toward a carefree life in nature.

examples.zh: 忙碌之余，真有几分濠濮间想。
examples.en: In the middle of all the bustle, I truly long for a quiet life by the water.

origin.source: 南朝宋·刘义庆《世说新语·言语》

story.en: When Emperor Jianwen of Jin entered the Hualin Garden he remarked that a place that touches the heart need not be far; a shaded spot with trees and water gives the feeling of the Hao and Pu rivers.
story.zh: 《世说新语·言语》载简文帝入华林园，说：“会心处不必在远，翳然林水，便自有濠、濮间想也。”

usage.en: Allusive and literary; 濠 háo, 濮 pú (rivers where Zhuangzi once fished and watched fish). Close to 濠梁之乐.
usage.zh: 典雅，“濠”读háo，“濮”读pú，指庄子曾观鱼、钓鱼的两条水。与“濠梁之乐”相近。

meaning.en: A place that does not exist; something that has vanished into nothing.
meaning.zh: 不存在的地方，指完全落空、化为乌有。

examples.zh: 多年的积蓄一夜之间都成了乌有之乡。
examples.en: Years of savings turned to nothing overnight.

examples.zh: 他向往的世外桃源，不过是乌有之乡。
examples.en: The paradise he longed for was only a place that does not exist.

usage.en: Literary; often as 化为乌有 in speech. Refers to non-existence or utopias.
usage.zh: 书面语，口语多说“化为乌有”，指不存在的地方或乌托邦。

story.en: Sima Xiangru's Zixu Fu stages a debate among three invented characters, Master Zixu, Master Wuyou ('Mr Nonexistent') and Lord Wushi. The name 'Wuyou xiansheng' gave rise to the later idiom for a nonexistent place or something vanished.
story.zh: 司马相如《子虚赋》假设“子虚先生”“乌有先生”“亡是公”三人问答，“乌有”即“何有”之意，虚构其人其事。后世由“乌有先生”引申出“乌有之乡”，指不存在的地方或消失殆尽的事物。
